title: 2. Freshness & Volume
description: Is the data arriving, and is there the right amount of it. Includes which clock each freshness number came from.

panels.title: Freshness lag per dataset
panels.description: Measured from the dataset's own clock. A dataset with no usable timestamp emits NO series rather than a zero - zero would read as perfectly fresh.

panels.title: Which clock was used
panels.description: event_time is the strongest evidence; object_mtime only proves a file was written, not that its contents are recent; unavailable means the dataset could not be measured at all.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT d.dataset_name AS "dataset",
                           f.timestamp_source AS "clock",
                           COALESCE(f.timestamp_column, '-') AS "column",
                           f.lag_seconds AS "lag_s",
                           f.status AS "status", f.severity AS "severity"
                    FROM (
                      SELECT DISTINCT ON (dataset_id) *
                      FROM freshness_checks ORDER BY dataset_id, checked_at DESC
                    ) f JOIN datasets d USING (dataset_id)
                    ORDER BY f.lag_seconds DESC NULLS FIRST

panels.title: Volume deviation from the rolling median
panels.description: Percent away from the median of comparable history. With same_day_type the baseline for a Saturday is built only from other weekend days, so a normal weekend dip sits near zero.

panels.title: Volume baseline detail
panels.description: `insufficient_history` means the baseline could not be computed from enough comparable points, so the check reports unknown and claims no threshold at all.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT d.dataset_name AS "dataset", v.row_count AS "rows",
                           v.baseline_method AS "method",
                           v.history_points || '/' || v.min_history_required AS "history",
                           v.baseline_median AS "median", v.baseline_mad AS "mad",
                           v.robust_z_score AS "robust_z",
                           v.deviation_percent AS "dev_pct",
                           CASE WHEN v.is_weekend THEN 'weekend' ELSE 'weekday' END AS "day_type",
                           v.status AS "status"
                    FROM (
                      SELECT DISTINCT ON (dataset_id) *
                      FROM volume_checks ORDER BY dataset_id, checked_at DESC
                    ) v JOIN datasets d USING (dataset_id)
                    ORDER BY abs(COALESCE(v.robust_z_score, 0)) DESC

panels.title: Row count history with the expected band
panels.description: The band is median +/- critical_z * spread, as recorded by the check. Drawn from the stored values rather than recomputed, so the picture matches the decision that was actually made.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT v.checked_at AS time, d.dataset_name AS metric,
                           v.row_count AS value
                    FROM volume_checks v JOIN datasets d USING (dataset_id)
                    WHERE $__timeFilter(v.checked_at)
                    ORDER BY v.checked_at
